text: All right. I want to thank everybody for joining us. I want to thank Mr. Graham for calling in and giving us some advice on the ordinance tonight. We can do whatever we want here, but we're surrounded by a much larger entity. So our focus should always be on our role as a city, as a small city and protecting our core services, making sure our police and fire are operating well, making sure our public works are, you know, our water's running, it's clean, making sure our toilets flush, all that great stuff. It's stuff that's behind the scenes, but it's stuff that can you imagine right now if we didn't have those services and you're stuck at home, that would be a nightmare. So city, you're doing a fantastic job of keeping that up and running. And we just have to remember our role as a city. We're not here to make judgments on exactly what every single person needs to do. I advise everyone to follow the policies that are guided by the CDC. Continue to wash your hands. If you're out in public and you have a cloth mask or any kind of mask, please, please protect yourself and protect others. If you're feeling sick, please do not go out and those sorts of things. If you need to get a test, you can call the county health department and arrange for a test. So continue to do that. As a city, of course we're protecting our core services, but the other half of what council does is budget. We're about to get into budget season. Seems like we're always in budget season. It always flies by these years. And we are in a better position as a city than most other cities, considering that we've had a reserve, we have a reserve, we've been fiscally conservative for many, many years, and we've always, in my experience, every time we have a budget retreat, we're always talking about some phantom disaster, some phantom emergency that we need to have this reserve for whatever reason. Did we know it was gonna be a pandemic? I don't think anybody knew that, but we've always had this phantom placeholder, what if situation, and this is definitely gonna be the, I think the standard, set the standard for what a disaster could possibly be, especially for the budget. We're gonna see an impact on our sales tax. I think we're in a better position as a city because we have a diversified revenue base with property and sales tax almost evenly split. There's a lot of cities out there that are very dependent on sales tax that are, I do not envy their upcoming budget sessions. That's gonna be a real hard conversation for cities that don't have, some cities don't have property tax. So I wanna commend past councils, past mayors, past city managers and our current city managers, current staff, current council for always having this mindset of worst case scenario. And when you budget from what is a worst case scenario could happen to us, this is the result. We're talking about a chicken ordinance when many other councils are not having that conversation. So great job there. We're gonna continue to make sure that our services, our core services for the city operate and they need to operate. We're gonna continue to take direction from the governor on what we can and cannot open, how we're going to reopen the steps that we're gonna take. And we're a very resilient city. The businesses, the way that they've reacted, there was a week or two there where it was panic for everybody and not knowing what's going on, but the way that our businesses have adapted, the way that they've adjusted to a complete shift and the way commerce happens is enviable. It's great to see what they're doing. Hopefully we don't have to continue for many more months in this, but we need to keep our eye on the prize of not overwhelming our healthcare resources. That's really been the goal of social distancing and all these impacts. It's not to hurt anybody. It's to flatten the curve and make sure that our healthcare services are not overwhelmed. And the simple stuff like breaking an arm, having a stroke, having a heart attack, the day-to-day emergencies that are crises for different families, that you have a hospital bed. That's the goal here. And we need to continue that.
